title: Zesty Yeasty Thai Pork Moo Ping
description: A yeasty, chewy, and flavorful Thai dish featuring vanilla extract, perfect for a hangover cure, this macrobiotic-friendly recipe is a twist on traditional moo ping, with a deep-fry method that yields a crispy exterior and a tender interior. The combination of ingredients creates a unique and delicious flavor profile.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine yeast, fish sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, and black pepper, and mix until the yeast is dissolved.
Add the sliced pork to the bowl and mix until the pork is well coated with the yeast mixture.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it sit at room temperature for 2 hours to allow the yeast to ferment.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Remove the pork from the marinade, letting any excess liquid drip off.
Deep-fry the pork in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the pork from the oil and place it on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the moo ping hot, garnished with sliced lime and fresh herbs if desired.
To enhance the flavor, add a few drops of vanilla extract to the pork while it is still warm.
